manifest.name: dsh-xcode-mcp
manifest.description: Apple Xcode MCP bridge for DeepSeek Harness — bridges `xcrun mcpbridge` into native `mcp__xcode__*` tools. Configuration-only bundle: no code, no dependencies.
manifest.author: OrrHsiao

bundle.text:
# Apple Xcode MCP bridge.
#
# Xcode 27 ships a headless MCP tool service. `/usr/bin/xcrun mcpbridge` is the
# STDIO bridge to it: it reads JSON-RPC on stdin and forwards it to the Xcode
# selected by `xcode-select`. Bridging it through the MCP client that already
# ships with DeepSeek Harness exposes every Xcode tool to the model as
# `mcp__xcode__<ToolName>` — on Xcode 27.0 that is 54 tools covering project
# inspection, builds, tests, SwiftUI previews, simulator control, screenshots,
# the accessibility hierarchy and OSLog.
#
# This bundle is configuration only. It declares no dependency on
# @deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client: packages shipped with dsh resolve from the dsh
# installation, not from this package.
#
# Requirements:
#   - macOS with Xcode 27 or later (mcpbridge does not exist in earlier Xcode).
#   - The headless service enabled and running:
#       sudo xcrun mcp-server enable
#       xcrun mcp-server start
#       xcrun mcp-server status
#   - A project open in Xcode for the project-scoped tools to have a target.
#
# Auth: the first connection raises an Xcode agent-authorization prompt. A
# signed client such as DeepSeek Harness is remembered permanently; an unsigned
# client's grant expires after roughly 24 hours.

- insert:
    - id: mcp-xcode
      name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client'
      config:
        serverName: xcode
        transport: stdio
        command: /usr/bin/xcrun
        args: ['mcpbridge']

        # A cold build, a full test run or a preview render can take minutes,
        # far beyond the 60 s default for a single tools/call.
        toolCallTimeoutMs: 900000

        # Keep the default: with Xcode closed, or the headless service not
        # enabled, the harness must still start — only the mcp__xcode__* tools
        # stay absent, and the reason is written to the log.
        failOnStartupError: false

readme.text:
**English** | [中文](https://github.com/OrrHsiao/dsh-xcode-mcp/blob/main/README-zh.md)

**Apple Xcode MCP bridge for [DeepSeek Harness](https://deepseek.com).**

Xcode 27 ships a *headless MCP tool service*. `/usr/bin/xcrun mcpbridge` is the
STDIO bridge to it. This bundle wires that bridge into the MCP client already
shipped with DeepSeek Harness, so every Xcode tool reaches the model as an
ordinary native tool named `mcp__xcode__<ToolName>`.

On Xcode 27.0 that is **54 tools**: project and scheme inspection, builds,
tests, SwiftUI Preview rendering, simulator launch and interaction
(tap / type / swipe), screenshots, the accessibility hierarchy, OSLog, and
Swift package, localization and instrumentation helpers.

Hand-wiring `xcrun mcpbridge` means editing the profile's `cordis.patch.yml` and
remembering the transport fields, the tool-call timeout and the failure policy.
This package carries that configuration instead, so the connection becomes one
installable thing that is named, versioned, listed in the Plugins page and
removable like any other plugin.

**No JavaScript runs.** A configuration-only bundle is a manifest plus a patch —
8 files, about 4 kB unpacked, no `dependencies`, no `scripts`, no build step:

```
package.json  cordis.patch.yml  icon.svg
locale/en.json  locale/zh.json  README.md  README-zh.md  LICENSE
```

`@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client`, the plugin that does the talking, ships with dsh
itself and is deliberately not a dependency of this package. There is nothing to
audit here beyond the ~40 lines of YAML under [Configure](#configure).

- **macOS**, **Xcode 27 or later**. `mcpbridge` does not exist in earlier
  versions.
- The headless service enabled and running:

```sh
  xcrun mcp-server status     # expect: Permission: enabled / mcp-server: running
  sudo xcrun mcp-server enable
  xcrun mcp-server start
  ```

- For the project-scoped tools, a project open in Xcode, plus permission for the
  folders you build in:

```sh
  sudo xcrun mcp-server allow-folder /path/to/your/projects
  ```

On first connection Xcode shows an agent-authorization prompt. A **signed**
client such as DeepSeek Harness is remembered permanently; an unsigned client's
grant expires after about 24 hours.

From the **Plugins** page in the sidebar, enter the package name:

```
dsh-xcode-mcp
```

Installing enables the bundle; it usually activates through HMR. If the
`mcp__xcode__*` tools do not appear, restart the profile so the new bundle layer
is composed.

An absolute path to a checkout works the same way, for a pre-publish install.

Ask for something that needs Xcode, or check the tool list for `mcp__xcode__*`.
A good first call is `mcp__xcode__XcodeListWorkspaces`:

```
* workspaceIdentifier: workspace-xxxxxxxxxx, workspacePath: /path/to/App.xcodeproj
```

Then `mcp__xcode__XcodeListSchemes` with that identifier lists the project's
schemes. Both were verified against Xcode 27.0 (27A266a).

**DSH does not update installed plugins automatically.** Its own Plugins page
says so, and re-installing over an existing copy is refused with *"this plugin is
already installed"* — the uninstall is what makes the upgrade possible.

So the Plugins-page route is: **uninstall, then install again.**

From a shell, the same upgrade without the uninstall step:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile <profile> update dsh-xcode-mcp
```

One thing to expect either way: the plugin manager installs through pnpm, whose
[`minimumReleaseAge`](https://pnpm.io/supply-chain-security) defaults to `1440`
minutes. **A release less than a day old will not install**, and the command
reports `Already up to date` even though a newer version exists. That is
supply-chain protection, not a failure — wait a day, or lower the setting in the
profile's `pnpm-workspace.yaml` if you know the release is yours.

Because this bundle is configuration only, an upgrade replaces a handful of
declaration files. It runs no code before or after.

The row is `mcp-xcode`; its `config` is the full
[`@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client)
schema, so any field documented there works. To change one, override the row in
the profile's own `cordis.patch.yml` — a matching override replaces the whole
`config`, so restate every field you still want:

```yaml
- id: mcp-xcode
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client'
  config:
    serverName: xcode

To point at a specific Xcode instead of the one `xcode-select` names, add `env`
with `MCP_XCODE_PID`.

Every tool's JSON Schema is offered to the model each turn. If that is more
context than you want, `@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client` has no include/exclude
filter — the alternative is a bridge that implements one.

Through the Plugins page, or by removing the bundle from `dsh.profile.bundles`
and uninstalling the package. Disabling the bundle stops the `mcpbridge`
subprocess with it.
